title: HandoffReady · actual local workflow
approval_actor: Agent-operated synthetic demonstration. Not customer or human trial evidence.
capture_note: Actual browser screens captured across an edited workflow; holds are editing durations, not measured inference latency.

slides.caption: A private delivery desk for web and design freelancers. This packet is synthetic.
Start with the agreed brief: a transparent logo, three distinct launch images and useful contact-email instructions.
Actual local Gemma inference proposes a checklist. The recording uses captured screens, not canned responses.
Review exact source quotations, formats and quantities before explicitly confirming the checklist.
Inspect real file bytes. Supported checks establish narrow facts, not aesthetic quality.
Three launch filenames contain only two distinct byte sequences. Renaming cannot create a third design.
Gemma runs locally again to propose associations. It never selects files or approves delivery automatically.
Suggestions remain unverified. Select and inspect the actual files before making an assessment.
Safeguard test: even a satisfied assessment cannot erase the opaque PNG’s failed transparency check.
The actual byte count fails: two distinct files, not the three requested. Dimensions can pass independently.
The guide contains only a welcome note. Operator review marks needs work; the manual check stays unknown.
The client manifest keeps failed and unresolved work visible. Raw source and private notes stay out.
Save and download an immutable JSON snapshot. Original delivery files must be sent separately.
Replace the opaque logo with actual transparent PNG bytes. A filename change alone would not fix it.
Changing the packet makes previous assessments stale. Explicitly review the current files again.
The new PNG passes the narrow alpha check after a fresh review. Final appearance still needs judgment.
The corrected logo passes; the duplicate launch image and incomplete guide still need work.
Earlier exports stay unchanged. A second download matched the original snapshot byte-for-byte.
Both snapshots remain available with their version context. Local AI assists; review controls the handoff.
